The record is outrunning the underlying play so far this season, and a new forward alone won't close that gap.

The defensive impact looks more durable than the scoring. We don't have a minutes projection to share, so watch who picks up his shifts if he sits.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't re-sign and has asked for a trade; Daily Faceoff carries the same report. The Athletic notes he is set to become an unrestricted free agent after this season.

What a team would be getting is a player still producing at the top of the league. Kucherov has four goals and 15 points in 12 games so far this season, and his results match his chances: his own expected goals (the quality of his shots) are 3.98 against four goals scored, so nothing here is luck. At five-on-five, Tampa Bay generates 57.61% of the expected goals while he is on the ice, and the team's share of the expected goals is 2.11 percentage points better with him out there. His 20.75 minutes a game and last season's 44 goals and 130 points fit the same picture.

For Tampa Bay, the timing matters. At 8-3-1, the Lightning control 56.9% of the expected goals as a team, so this is a contender deciding whether to move its best player. For fantasy managers, the trade ask adds uncertainty about where he lands, but the underlying numbers give no reason to doubt his output.

Our numbers say the Canucks lose a player who was not producing much so far this season. Chytil has no goals and two points in seven games despite 19.89 minutes a night, and his own expected goals (the quality of his chances) came to 1.15, so he is 1.15 goals short of what those chances suggest. That points to some bad luck, but the bigger concern is that Vancouver controlled only 29 percent of the expected goals when he was on the ice at five-on-five, and the team's share was 12.44 points better without him. The Canucks sit at 3-11-1 and have created just 39 percent of the expected goals overall, so the problem runs deeper than one forward. Going by how the coach has used his players, Elias Pettersson (20:35 a night) is next in line for Chytil's minutes. As Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis posted, an ex-Maple Leaf is likely to make his Canucks debut against his former team.

Manson's loss shows up less in his scoring than in how Colorado plays when he's out there. He has four points in 13 games and has scored about half a goal more than the quality of his own chances would predict, which is a small sample. At 5-on-5 the Avalanche had 48.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, against 53% for the team overall, and the team's share is about 5.5 points better when he sits. So we wouldn't read this as the loss of a driver. Colorado is also better than its 7-5-1 record suggests, with 54.3% of expected goals so far this season, and its goaltending has cost it about 4.3 goals against what the shots called for. That is the bigger swing factor. Manson plays 15 minutes a night, so the drop-off will come from Juulsen's play, not from a hole in the lineup. We haven't got a read yet on who absorbs his minutes.

Calgary can ill afford more attrition. The Flames are 5-7-0 and have taken 46.7% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, and their goalies have saved 5.5 goals fewer than expected, which has made a middling process look worse. Othmann, drafted 16th overall by the Rangers in 2021 and a 29-goal OHL scorer in 2022-23 for Flint, hasn't helped yet. He has no points in six games, averaging 9.33 minutes. His 35.58% share of expected goals at five-on-five is well below the team's 47%, and Calgary has fared 13.21 percentage points worse with him on the ice. His own 0.29 expected goals match his zero goals closely, so this isn't bad luck; the chances just haven't come. Our model puts him at 0.59 expected goals per 60 minutes, a modest ceiling. His absence costs the Flames little on the ice, but with Cooley and Zary also out, the depth is thin, and fantasy managers can safely let him go.

ANA sits at 46.7% of expected goals and 44% at five-on-five, with goalies 3 goals below expected, so a 5-7-1 record looks about right. Scoring runs hot, defense runs thin, and that's an uneasy mix for both sides.

Cooley has 4 goals against 3.35 expected from his own shots, so he is scoring about as often as his chances say he should, and he is taking 56.71% of five-on-five chances while on the ice. Sergachev is the bigger overperformer: 3 goals on 1.59 expected, and his 15 points in 13 games put him ahead of last season's pace of 59 over 78. We wouldn't bank on that goal total holding, but his 58.12% share at five-on-five and 23.38 minutes a night show a real role. stories.take:
The Hockey News' Morning Skate reports that Calgary goalie Devin Cooley was injured in the Oilers' win over the Flames, and that Sergei Bobrovsky struggled against Seattle. The write-up doesn't say how serious Cooley's injury is.

If he's out, it hurts. Cooley has been a bright spot in a rough start for CGY. His goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average goalie facing the same shots) is +2.19 in seven games so far this season, on top of a .912 save percentage. Last year he was +17.23 over 31 games. As a team, Calgary sits at -5.5 in that measure and is 5-7-0, so the goaltending has not been the problem when he plays. Without him, that picture could change quickly.

Bobrovsky's .885 save percentage looks ugly, but his goals saved above expected is +0.92 in 10 games, so he has been a bit better than the shots he's faced. That's a far cry from last season's -13.5 over 52 games. We'd call this a slow start with some luck-adjusted support, not proof the decline is over.

He is also 30 and had 20 points in 53 games last year, so there is no big offensive history to lean on. For fantasy, he is a drop in most formats. moves.take: Dallas announced it placed forward Matt Duchene on long-term injured reserve, retroactive to Sept. 29, and recalled forwards Arttu Hyry and Colin Blackwell from Texas (AHL). Hyry, who kills penalties on the third line, has three goals this season, about 1.2 more than his chances would predict, and Dallas controls more of the chance quality when he plays at even strength. Blackwell has gone without a point and the team has done worse with him on the ice. Going by how the coach has used his players, Oskar Bäck is next in line for Duchene's minutes.

moves.take: EDM announced it placed Ryan Nugent-Hopkins on injured reserve, placed Alec Regula on long-term injured reserve and recalled Josh Samanski under emergency conditions. Nugent-Hopkins has played 19.95 minutes a night, mostly on the second line and the first power-play unit, so Owen Michaels (12:49 a night) is next in line for his minutes and Kasperi Kapanen is the likeliest to move up on the power play. Samanski has averaged 7.73 minutes in six games, so this is a much smaller role. The Oilers are 8-2-1, and their even-strength expected goal share is 49%.
